versions: Properties of Boron
answer:
● Covalent Bonds
● High Melting Point
● Icosahedral 3D Structure
● 4 Max Covalency (Although Group has Max 6)

versions: Explain the structure of Diborane (B₂H₆) with bond lengths and bond angles.
answer:
● Diborane: B₂H₆ has 4 terminal B–H bonds and 2 bridging B–H–B bonds.
● B₂H₆ is a planar molecule.
● Terminal B–H = 119 pm, bridge B–H = 134 pm
● ∠H–B–H ≈ 120°, ∠B–H–B ≈ 97°
● The two bridge bonds are 3-centre-2-electron (3c–2e) bonds.

versions: Explain the structure and formation of AlCl₃ and compare its nature with AlF₃ and Why BCl₃ does not form a dimer?
answer:
● Al₂O₃ + C + Cl₂ → Al₂Cl₆ + CO (Reductive Chlorination)
● AlCl₃ forms a dimer with two bridging Cl atoms.
● AlCl₃ is covalent due to high polarising power of Al³⁺, whereas AlF₃ is predominantly ionic.
● Due to large size of Cl, B cannot handle 4 Cl atoms

versions: Write the disproportionation reaction of AlCl.
answer: 3AlCl → 2Al + AlCl₃

versions: Explain the reactivity of Group 13 elements towards air.
answer:
● 4M + 3O₂ → 2M₂O₃
● B is unreactive in crystalline form (reacts in amorphous form).
● Al forms a protective Al₂O₃ layer (reacts if layer is removed).
● Ga, In: No reaction.

versions: Explain the reactivity of Group 13 elements towards N₂.
answer:
● 2M + N₂ → 2MN
● B: Heating
● Al, Ga, In: Strong Heating
● Tl: No Reaction

versions: Explain Back Bonding in Group 13 halides and its effect on acidic nature.
answer:
● Backbonding: BF₃ > BCl₃ > BBr₃ > BI₃
● Acidic Nature: BF₃ < BCl₃ < BBr₃ < BI₃
● Back bonding provides e⁻ to B, making it less acidic.

versions: Explain the nature of oxides of Group 13 elements.
answer:
● B₂O₃ is acidic.
● Al₂O₃ and Ga₂O₃ are amphoteric.
● In₂O₃ and Tl₂O₃ are basic.
● Basic character increases down the group.

versions: Write the properties and structure of Boric Acid (H₃BO₃).
answer:
● H₃BO₃ or B(OH)₃ is a weak monobasic Lewis acid.
● It has 3 OH connected to one Boron.
● B(OH)₃ + 2H₂O ⇌ [B(OH)₄]⁻ + H₃O⁺ (Non Protic Acid).
● Solid at Room Temp => Hydrogen Bonding

versions: Write the properties and formation of trihalides of Group 13 and explain their hydrolysis.
answer:
● Trihalides have general formula MX₃ and are generally covalent and electron deficient.
● 2M + 3X₂ → 2MX₃
● Hydrolysed Easily →
B forms [B(OH)₄]⁻, Others form [M(H₂O)₆]⁺³

versions: Write two methods for the preparation of Diborane (B₂H₆).
